- [2023/05/21] The appellant argued they were not responsible for installing flashing around windows due to specific contractual terms.
- [2023/05/21] The respondents claimed the contract terms were superseded by a Deed, specifically clause 14, which constituted the entire agreement.
- [2023/05/21] The appellant referenced clause 7 of the Deed, arguing it preserved the original contract terms.
- [2023/05/21] The Tribunal preferred Mr. Brennan's expert evidence over Mr. Sim's regarding the necessity of flashing for windows.
- [2023/05/21] Mr. Brennan's report indicated windows leaked due to the absence of small joint sealer and flashing.
- [2023/05/21] Mr. Sim argued flashing was unnecessary due to the use of commercial-grade window sections with sub-heads and sub-sills.
- [2023/05/21] The Tribunal concluded the windows were defective due to the absence of small joint sealant, requiring replacement.
- [2023/05/21] The Tribunal found the responsibility for flashing was not relevant to the appellant's responsibility for window replacement costs.
- [2023/05/21] The Tribunal rejected ground 1, finding no error of law or unfair conclusion.
